\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{تنہا} (tanhā)}{تنہا (tanhā)}]{\ur{تنہا} (tanhā) — lonely; alone}

\label{lesson:UR-C450-tanha}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to cling tightly, then the Urdu for passionate love.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{تنہا}}
\textbf{\ur{تنہا}} — \emph{tanhā} — \textquotedblleft{}lonely; alone\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{شہر} \ur{میں} \ur{نانی} \ur{بالکل} \ur{تنہا} \ur{ہیں۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{shahr meṅ nānī bilkul tanhā haiṅ.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
In the city my granny is all alone.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{تنہا}} (\emph{tanhā}) is usually traced to Persian \emph{tanhā}, \textquotedblleft{}alone\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tanhā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tanhā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{shahr meṅ nānī bilkul tanhā haiṅ.} — In the city my granny is all alone.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for to cling tightly, then the Urdu for passionate love, then say \emph{tanhā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{اکیلا} (akelā)}{اکیلا (akelā)}]{\ur{اکیلا} (akelā) — on one's own}

\label{lesson:UR-C450-akela}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for passionate love, then the Urdu for lonely.

\textbf{\ur{اکیلا}} — \emph{akelā} — \textquotedblleft{}on one's own\textquotedblright{}.

\end{quote}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{جدائی} (judāī)}{جدائی (judāī)}]{\ur{جدائی} (judāī) — separation (from someone dear)}

\label{lesson:UR-C450-judai}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for lonely, then the Urdu for on one's own.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{جدائی}}
\textbf{\ur{جدائی}} — \emph{judāī} — \textquotedblleft{}separation (from someone dear)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{بہن} \ur{کی} \ur{جدائی} \ur{میں} \ur{وہ} \ur{روتی} \ur{ہے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{bahan kī judāī meṅ voh rotī hai.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
She cries because her sister is far away.
\end{quote}

Feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{جدائی}} (\emph{judāī}) is usually traced to Persian \emph{judāī}, \textquotedblleft{}separation\textquotedblright{}, built on \emph{judā}, \textquotedblleft{}apart\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{بسورنا} (bisūrnā)}{بسورنا (bisūrnā)}]{\ur{بسورنا} (bisūrnā) — to whimper; to pull a crying face}

\label{lesson:UR-C450-bisurna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for on one's own, then the Urdu for separation.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{بسورنا}}
\textbf{\ur{بسورنا}} — \emph{bisūrnā} — \textquotedblleft{}to whimper; to pull a crying face\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{ماں} \ur{کے} \ur{جانے} \ur{پر} \ur{بچہ} \ur{بسور} \ur{رہا} \ur{تھا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{māṅ ke jāne par bachchā bisūr rahā thā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
When his mother left, the child was whimpering.
\end{quote}

Past (she …): \ur{وہ} \ur{دیر} \ur{تک} \ur{بسوری}, \emph{voh der tak bisūrī}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{بسورنا}} (\emph{bisūrnā}) is inherited: CDIAL lists the Hindi cousin \emph{bisūrnā}, \textquotedblleft{}to put on a crying face\textquotedblright{}, under \emph{viśūratē}, \textquotedblleft{}is hurt, is distressed\textquotedblright{}, a form it reconstructs (CDIAL 11941).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{اوجھل} (ojhal)}{اوجھل (ojhal)}]{\ur{اوجھل} (ojhal) — out of sight}

\label{lesson:UR-C450-ojhal}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for separation, then the Urdu for to whimper.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{اوجھل}}
\textbf{\ur{اوجھل}} — \emph{ojhal} — \textquotedblleft{}out of sight\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{ریل} \ur{گاڑی} \ur{دور} \ur{جا} \ur{کر} \ur{اوجھل} \ur{ہو} \ur{گئی۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{rel gāṛī dūr jā kar ojhal ho gaī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The train went far off and disappeared from sight.
\end{quote}

\textbf{\ur{اوجھل}} (\emph{ojhal}) is inherited from \emph{ōjjhalla}, \textquotedblleft{}a screen, a veil\textquotedblright{}, a form CDIAL reconstructs (CDIAL 2542).
\end{cousinweb}
